title: Causal Chain of Runtime Supply Chain Attack: Targeting the Context Ingestion Link

original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain of Runtime Supply Chain Attack: Targeting the Context Ingestion Link

**Problem:** Jiang et al. 2026 describes a runtime supply chain attack chain: external source → malicious content delivery → context ingestion → instruction execution. The context ingestion link (the moment injected instructions become part of the agent's context) is under-studied.

**Direction:** Instrument an agent to log the exact moment malicious instructions enter the context window and the subsequent instruction execution. Test whether inserting a context sanitization step between ingestion and execution — using a simple rule-based filter — breaks the chain without degrading benign task performance.

**Why it matters:** If a context sanitization step between ingestion and execution can break the attack chain with low false-positive cost, it is a cheap, deployable defense.

**Relevant context:** Jiang et al. 2026 supply chain attack chain; RAG security; context sanitization research.
